title: Rotate Image
description:
You are given an `n x n` 2D integer `matrix` representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees clockwise.

You must rotate the image **in-place**, meaning you have to modify the input 2D `matrix` directly without allocating another 2D matrix to perform the rotation.
hints: Element (r, c) moves to position (c, n - 1 - r) after a 90-degree clockwise rotation.
You can decompose a 90-degree clockwise rotation into two simple in-place operations: transpose the matrix across its main diagonal, then reverse every row.
Alternatively, rotate four symmetric cells at a time ring by ring from the outer layer inward.

examples.explanation: Each row becomes a column from right to left: row 0 [1,2,3] becomes the last column.
Both the outer 4x4 ring and the inner 2x2 ring rotate 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
